scope: P4.4 native Qwen delegation capacity exhaustion

verification.regression: New real-SQLite test timed out before the fix (6 passed, 1 failed); all 7 invocation tests pass after the fix, including unchanged same-key cancelled retry.
commands: pnpm exec turbo run test --filter=@bb/server -- test/security/control-plane
verification.dockerCommand: BB_CONTROL_PLANE_BROWSER_ARTIFACTS="$BB_THREAD_STORAGE/p4-capacity-browser" BB_TEST_BROWSER_CHANNEL=chrome caffeinate -i pnpm exec turbo run test:control-plane-deployment --filter=@bb/server --env-mode=loose -- --browser-only
notes: Each user runs with a native one-slot parent/child wait, explicit cancellation, expiry, a successful leaf at the unchanged one-slot limit, then successful delegation at two slots. Actual UID/HOME/cwd and foreign result denial are checked.
Deadline expiry is accelerated only by a test executable aging the private database reservation. The production deadline stays 600000 ms; this is not a ten-minute wall-clock soak.
Cancelled native queue messages may remain inspectable; background sends return 409 run_is_not_chat and cancelled children produce no execution files after capacity is restored.
The test restores the original host override. Docker resources and live BB limits are unchanged.

Earlier fixture assertions incorrectly expected queue deletion and HTTP 403 for background sends. Those runs did not count as acceptance; the final full deployment passed with the actual native contracts.

decision: No automatic child-slot reservation or concurrency bypass. Bounded cancellation/deadline failure is supported under saturation. Guaranteed progress needs a separate parent admission policy; operational headroom alone cannot guarantee it.
limitations: Verified with stock Qwen and the deterministic test model, not corporate-fork authorization.
